audit_scope.description: Trust model analysis for Ethereum protocol specifications including EIP-7636 (Client ENR Entry), EIP-160 (EXP Gas Repricing), Cancun System Instructions, and EIP-8070 (Sparse Blobpool)

components.name: Execution Layer (EL)
interfaces: EVM Opcode Execution (CREATE, CALL, RETURN, REVERT, SELFDESTRUCT, EXP)

trusted_external_entities.name: Node Operator
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Node operators configure their own nodes and have administrative control over client settings including client identity disclosure. They are semi-trusted as they control the node but their configuration choices can affect network-level information disclosure.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer Node
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peer nodes on the Ethereum P2P network are untrusted external entities. They can send arbitrary ENR records, transaction announcements, and blob data. All data from peers must be validated before use.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Peer Node
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Explicitly malicious peer nodes attempting to send falsified client identity information, corrupt blob data, or perform selective withholding attacks. Represents the adversarial model for peer interactions.

trusted_external_entities.name: Provider Peer (Blob Data)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peer nodes claiming to have full blob data (provider role in EIP-8070). They are untrusted and must be validated via sampling noise to detect selective withholding or data corruption.

trusted_external_entities.name: Contract Caller / External Transaction Sender
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External parties submitting transactions that execute smart contract code including EXP opcode and other EVM operations. They are untrusted and can submit malicious transactions attempting DoS or exploits.

trusted_external_entities.name: DoS Attacker
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Malicious actor attempting computational DoS attacks via underpriced opcodes (e.g., EXP before EIP-160) or other resource exhaustion vectors. Represents the adversarial model for transaction processing.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: ENR records from peers are untrusted and self-reported. Client identity information cannot be verified and must never be used for security-critical decisions. The 'client' field is treated as informational only for network analytics.
Malicious peers can send arbitrary falsified client identity information. The system must mark all ENR client data as untrusted and prevent its use in access control or security decisions.

Node operators have legitimate administrative access to configure client identity disclosure settings. Their configuration choices are trusted for their own node but do not affect trust in data from other peers.
Blob transaction announcements from peers are untrusted. Cell masks and transaction hashes must be validated. Nodes use probabilistic sampling to verify data availability.

Provider peers claiming to have full blob data are untrusted. Samplers include noise columns (C_extra=1 random column) to detect selective withholding. Missing noise columns indicate potential misbehavior.
All blob data from providers must be validated per EIP-7594 before propagation. Providers that fail noise column tests may be flagged for misbehavior and potentially disconnected.

External transactions containing contract calls with EXP opcode are untrusted. Gas costs must be correctly calculated based on exponent byte length (10 + 50*bytes post-EIP-160) to prevent computational DoS.

Attackers can craft transactions with many EXP operations using large exponents. The 5x gas cost increase (from 10 to 50 gas per byte) post-Spurious Dragon mitigates DoS by making attacks economically unviable.

Transactions containing CREATE/CREATE2 opcodes from external callers are untrusted. Init code size limits, address collision checks, balance verification, depth limits (1024), and nonce overflow checks must all be enforced before contract creation.

Transactions containing CALL/CALLCODE/DELEGATECALL/STATICCALL from external callers are untrusted. Static context violations, depth limits, balance checks, and gas calculations (including cold/warm access costs) must be validated to prevent attacks.

SELFDESTRUCT operations triggered by external transactions are constrained by EIP-6780. Only contracts created in the same transaction can be deleted, preventing abuse of the selfdestruct mechanism to manipulate state in unexpected ways.
